title: Tseitin size on all graphs reduces to cellular-or-compact minors, and block-scrambled wall networks defeat the compact case
subject: Size lower bounds for resolution and PCR refutations of Tseitin formulas on all graphs
conclusion: Resolution and PCR size of Tseitin formulas transfers along weak immersions and topological minors, giving 2^Omega(tw^(1/9)/polylog) on every graph and reducing 2^Omega(tw/polylog) to finding a cellular or compact topological minor of nearly full treewidth in every subcubic graph, where immersions add nothing. On walls joined by block-scrambled bundles along an expander, no compact minor keeps the treewidth and cells exist only at scale sqrt(b), a candidate counterexample.
